- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in bullish sentiment periods; apply a 1–2% downward bias to final forecast if sentiment >0.67 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is bullish but price is flat or declining, model often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
